Hi Aisha,

Great — thanks. We prefer DNS TXT-based attestation for our private zones because our change control is faster for TXT records than spinning signed JWTs. Attached are: acme-hostlist.csv and acme-csr-examples.txt. The hostlist includes our on-prem LB FQDNs and the service IPs behind them.

About TLS termination: our current plan is to terminate external TLS at our on-prem LB, and then use client mTLS from the LB to Redwood for the private API calls (we want mutual authentication). That means Redwood would present a trust anchor for client cert validation, and we will present client certs generated by our internal CA.

Questions:
- What exact proof format do you require in the TXT entry (key name + base64 signature)?
- Do you support OCSP stapling for certificates Redwood issues?
- We would like certificate rotation cadence recommendations (we typically prefer 90-day leaf certs).

Janet Lawson
Dir, Cloud Engineering — Acme Energy
janet.lawson@acme-energy.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Host attestation & client mTLS transition for Acme Energy private deployment

Janet — thanks for the files, that helps. A few technical clarifications from our side: 

- TXT proof format: we accept a simple key:value TXT under _redwood-assert.<fqdn> where the value is a base64-encoded signature of the FQDN + timestamp using a key you control. Example key: "redwood_v1=BASE64SIG". We also accept a CSR signed by your internal CA if you prefer.

- OCSP: Redwood-managed certificates support OCSP stapling for edge-terminated certs. For the mTLS link (if you terminate at your LB and we do client-auth on our side), we expect client certs to be verifiable by a CA chain you provide; we can check CRLs/OCSP if you publish them, but for private CAs we typically validate by pinning the intermediate or presenting a trusted root via our truststore for that account.

- Rotation: 90 days is fine for leaf certs. For the mTLS client certs we recommend a rotation window of 60–90 days with automated renewal if you can support ACME/SCEP workflows. For the trust anchor (root/intermediate) we recommend a 3–5 year cadence unless you have key compromise concerns.

I've attached a short primer (redwood-mtls-options.pdf) that compares the approaches and outlines tradeoffs (latency, revocation checks, audit surface).

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm TXT format (if OK we'll provide a sample DNS record for one FQDN).
2) We produce a 1-page MAP including rotation cadence and responsibilities.
3) Schedule the onboarding call (I can lead the implementation portion).

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood-mtls-options.pdf]

Subject: Re: Host attestation & client mTLS transition for Acme Energy private deployment

Adding a few specifics for the MAP and our security questionnaire:

- Trust anchor handling: Redwood can either: (A) host your root/intermediate in our per-customer truststore (read-only, with HSM-protected keys for any re-issuing), or (B) we can accept leaf certs signed by your CA without storing your CA. Option A helps with automated validation and short-lived cert issuance from Redwood for internal components; Option B reduces shared secrets but requires you to push CSRs or use ACME to generate certs.

- Attestation proof options we support: DNS TXT (short-lifetime TXT, TTL 300), CSR signed + out-of-band challenge, or ATS-signed JWT pulled from your attestation endpoint. For DNS TXT we recommend including a time-limited nonce and an signature: e.g. _redwood-assert.example.internal TXT "redwood_v1:base64(sig)|ts=20271112T1200Z".

- OCSP/CRL: if you want real-time revocation checks for client certs we can configure on-call stapling checks but for most private CA flows we rely on short rotation + CRL snapshots pushed to Redwood S3 endpoints. If you require near-zero risk we can run OCSP responders in your VPC via a Peered proxy.

- Audit: we will add the following log entries to your audit stream: cert-issue, cert-rotate, attestation-verify, and tls-handshake-failure with correlation IDs. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (syslog/Fluentd endpoint).

Please confirm whether you prefer Redwood-hosted truststore (Option A) or push-only (Option B). Also confirm acceptance of the DNS TXT nonce format and TTL. Once confirmed we'll circulate the MAP PDF with task owners.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Host attestation & client mTLS transition for Acme Energy private deployment

Rishi / team — thanks, that all sounds reasonable. We choose:

- DNS TXT attestation using the nonce format you suggested (TTL 300) — we can automate short-life TXT creation in our pipeline.
- Option B for the trust anchor: we will not host our root in Redwood's truststore; instead we will push CSRs and manage our CA.
- Rotation: we'll do 90-day leaf certs for service identities and 365-day intermediate lifecycle; client certs will rotate 60 days.

Please go ahead and draft the MAP including: responsibilities for adding TXT proof, CSR exchange process, vault/KMS pointers, and rollback plan if a cert chain fails. Also include the verification steps you will run during the onboarding call.

We can take the onboarding call on Tue 11/16 at 10:00 PT — that works for our SREs.

Janet
